A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 24 readable pages including Appendix A.1–A.11. Text, equations, figures, and tables support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, goal-parameter ablations, and appendix analyses of network depth, batch size, and discretization.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the classification comparisons in Figures 3–4 and supplementary experiments in the appendix.

M1.justification: The PID-based objectives, three input classes, activation functions, network setups, and training procedures remain identical in Sections 2–4 and Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MNIST and CIFAR-10 classification tasks and retain the same label-context and feedback scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 3 and 8 retain the same backpropagation, random-projection, readout-only, and bivariate infomorphic comparisons. Comparator participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: The validation splits, training budgets, model configurations, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. This includes Table 1's main settings and Appendix A.11's batch-size and bin-count protocols.

E4.justification: The goal-parameter ablations, convergence diagnostics, recurrence analysis, deeper-network experiments, and batch-size/bin-count sensitivity analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 10-run minimum–maximum intervals in Figures 3–4, repeated hyperparameter optimizations in Appendix A.6, and initialization counts in Appendix A.11.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Figure 4 retains 92.8% versus 94.9% MNIST accuracy for heuristic versus optimized goals, and 42.5% CIFAR-10 accuracy versus 42.2% for backpropagation.

T1.justification: The PID definitions, objective equations, shared-exclusion redundancy formulation, and trivariate consistency equations remain unchanged, including Appendices A.2 and A.7.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about interpretable local learning, three-input infomorphic neurons, and performance comparable to backpropagation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of important PID atoms and sparse connectivity are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same qualifications about network depth, discrete PID, and biological implementation.

D1.justification: The training pseudocode, software, hardware, compute-time estimates, hyperparameters, data-split descriptions, and code-access information are identical in the main text and Appendices A.1, A.3, and A.4.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to earlier bivariate infomorphic networks, coherent infomax, and other local learning approaches.

P1.justification: v5 combines two pairs of introductory paragraphs, adjusts author-footnote spacing, and adds publication-header text. Scientific wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds the ICLR 2025 running header, updates the arXiv margin stamp, and slightly reflows pages 2–5. Figures and tables are unchanged; page bodies 6–24 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: v5 makes limited publication and formatting updates while retaining all methods, evidence, explanations, and limitations, including the appendices. These edits establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
